advances: The convex-completion escape model in the preceding obstacle is impossible for a reason independent of its designated finite ledger. For every actual base-dimension-two convex body, after every convexity-created positive integer fiber is included and the canonical half-strength product reservoir is recomputed from those actual fiber volumes, the global complete metronoid-core capacity satisfies \(G\ge Q/8\). Hence every body \(\widetilde C_M\) in that model satisfies the first completion alternative \(G(\widetilde C_M)\ge Q(\widetilde C_M)/100\), with substantial slack. No load-minimal optimizer, synchronized thinning, greedy order, or collision convention can restore the proposed counterexample after completion. This eliminates the explicit completion model; it does not assert the registered greedy-simplex conclusion in base dimension at least three.
author: research-agent
proof:
All quantities in (1)-(3) are computed from the actual completed body \(C\); no designated pre-completion fiber volume is used.

Apply accepted fact 8aac56c49321466c with the affine subspace \(A=\mathbb R^2\). In its notation,
\[
 D_A=I_+,
 \qquad
 B=\operatorname{aff}(I_+),
 \qquad
 q:=\dim B\in\{0,1,2\},
 \qquad
 W_A=W.
\tag{8}
\]
Its support-free global consequence gives
\[
 G\ge\frac1{64}
 \min\{W,2^{2-q}W_A\}.
\tag{9}
\]
Since \(W_A=W\) and \(2^{2-q}\ge1\), equation (9) becomes
\[
 G\ge\frac W{64}.
\tag{10}
\]
This includes support ranks zero and one as well as full planar support; there is no hidden no-rank-drop premise.

It remains to compare the actual product reservoir with \(W\). Fix a good parity class \(\xi\). Directly from (3), its reservoir contribution is
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 Q_\xi
 &:=\sum_{\substack{\{u,v\}:u\ne v\\u\equiv v\equiv\xi}}
 \frac{a_ua_v}{4A_\xi}\\
 &=\frac1{8A_\xi}
 \left(A_\xi^2-
 \sum_{z\equiv\xi}a_z^2\right)
 \le\frac{A_\xi}{8}.
 \end{aligned}
\tag{11}
\]
Bad and empty classes contribute zero. The parity classes are disjoint, so summing (11) over the good classes gives
\[
 Q=\sum_{\xi\ \mathrm{good}}Q_\xi
 \le\frac18
 \sum_{\xi\ \mathrm{good}}A_\xi
 \le\frac W8.
\tag{12}
\]
Combining (10) and (12) yields
\[
 G\ge\frac W{64}
 \ge\frac18Q,
\tag{13}
\]
which proves (4). If \(Q>0\), then \(Q/8>Q/100\), proving (5). The case \(Q=0\) was already noted.

For (6), compactness and convexity are immediate. If the \(y_j\) span \(\mathbb R^2\), their convex hull has nonempty planar interior, while \(K\) has nonempty \(d\)-dimensional interior; hence \(\widetilde C_M\) is full-dimensional. Its compact base projection contains only finitely many integer bases, so its actual \(W\), parity masses, reservoir \(Q\), and capacity \(G\) are exactly within the scope of (1)-(5). Every convexity-created positive integer fiber contributes to the actual \(a_z\) and hence to both sides of (12). The proof never retains the obsolete designated value \(a\), never reuses the designated finite reservoir after completion, and never assumes that first-generation midpoint targets remain collision-free.

Finally, a load-minimal optimizer, the synchronized whole-label atlas, physical target aggregation, and the greedy rank-raising order are all downstream of the actual reservoir. Equation (13) already proves the complete-core terminal before any of those choices are made. Therefore recomputing them cannot change the first-alternative conclusion, and no second greedy-simplex alternative is required for the bodies (6). The argument is restricted to base dimension two and makes no rank-uniform claim for the unresolved branch in higher base dimension.
statement:
Let \(d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^2\times\mathbb R^d\) be a convex body with positive total mixed-integer fiber volume, and use the actual completed fiber profile
\[
 C_z:=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:(z,x)\in C\},
 \qquad
 a_z:=\operatorname{vol}_d(C_z),
 \qquad
 I_+:=\{z\in\mathbb Z^2:a_z>0\},
 \qquad
 W:=\sum_{z\in I_+}a_z>0.
\tag{1}
\]
Let \(G=\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{core}}(C)\) be the global complete metronoid-core capacity in the normalization of accepted fact 8aac56c49321466c. For every parity class \(\xi\in(\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z)^2\), put
\[
 A_\xi:=\sum_{z\equiv\xi\ (\mathrm{mod}\ 2)}a_z,
 \qquad
 M_\xi:=\max_{z\equiv\xi\ (\mathrm{mod}\ 2)}a_z,
\tag{2}
\]
where an empty class has \(A_\xi=M_\xi=0\). Call \(\xi\) good when \(A_\xi>0\) and \(M_\xi\le A_\xi/4\), and define the actual half-strength canonical product reservoir of accepted fact 036a276c54ec5e66 by
\[
 r_{\{u,v\}}:=
 \begin{cases}
 \dfrac{a_ua_v}{4A_\xi},
 &u\ne v,\quad u\equiv v\equiv\xi,\quad \xi\text{ good},\\[2mm]
 0,&\text{otherwise},
 \end{cases}
 \qquad
 Q:=\sum_{\{u,v\}}r_{\{u,v\}}.
\tag{3}
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{G\ge\frac W{64}\ge\frac Q8.}
\tag{4}
\]
Consequently, if \(Q>0\), then
\[
 \boxed{G>\frac Q{100}.}
\tag{5}
\]
If \(Q=0\), the weak first alternative \(G\ge Q/100\) is automatic.

In particular, fix any \(M\ge3\), any centrally symmetric \(d\)-dimensional convex body \(K\), and any finite data \(y_j\in\mathbb Z^2\), \(c_j\in\mathbb R^d\), and form
\[
 \widetilde C_M
 :=\operatorname{conv}
 \bigcup_{j=1}^M
 \bigl(\{y_j\}\times(c_j+K)\bigr).
\tag{6}
\]
Whenever the base points span \(\mathbb R^2\), this is a convex body in \(\mathbb R^2\times\mathbb R^d\). Equations (4)-(5) apply to the complete actual fiber profile of \(\widetilde C_M\), including every convexity-created integer fiber. Thus the specific moment-curve bodies in the preceding completion test always satisfy
\[
 G(\widetilde C_M)\ge\frac18Q(\widetilde C_M)
 >\frac1{100}Q(\widetilde C_M)
\tag{7}
\]
when their actual \(Q\) is positive.
